title: Three Weeks and One Short Chart
subtitle: 医学药研 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 医学药研（科学与技术·医学与健康科学）
meta: 主题语境：医学药研（科学与技术·医学与健康科学）　|　核心词汇：flu　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flu 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the nurse ① caught the flu that no doctor in the ward would have recorded, and she said the catching was the whole of the winter. The ② flu, meaning the illness itself and not the fever, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; the flu, she said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ case of flu in that ward had the same short chart beside it, and the ④ flu at the far bed, meaning the part they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only part anybody ever thanked twice. The flu, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the nurse said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flu was the whole of the matter, meaning the season and not the illness. The ⑥ flu, meaning the season and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; flu, he said, is either something you catch or the only word that means both an illness and a season. He said the season is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ flu had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short chart. The ⑧ flu of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in February, was one ward and three weeks of recording; flu, she said, is either the part at the far bed or the reason you learned to record. She said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flu I remember is the part recorded in the plan, which closed in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the ward. ⑩ Flu, my mother said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all flu, she said, is a season that has agreed to look like an illness. She said the season was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 流感（指病房里每一个病例旁边的那一个）
B. n. 流感（指那一场本身，与发热症状相对）
C. 固定搭配：catch the flu 染上流感
D. n. 流感（指留给孩子们的那一部分）
E. n. 流感（抽象总称，指一间病房的流感之事）
F. n. 流感（指计划里写到、被记录过的那一部分）
G. n. 流感季；流行期（指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 流行期（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: caught the flu that no doctor in the ward would have recorded
The flu, meaning the illness itself and not the fever
Every case of flu in that ward
the flu at the far bed
the flu was the whole of the matter
the flu had become a line in a plan
The flu of the whole thing

answers.why: catch the flu 意为“染上流感”，1968 年那位护士染上了一场病房里没有一位医生肯记录的流感。
flu 意为“流感”，指那一场本身而不是发热症状，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记录。
flu 意为“流感”，指病房里每一个病例旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张短短的病历表。
flu 意为“流感”，指留给孩子们的那一部分，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flu 意为“流感季、流行期”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这个流感季就是那件事的全部。
flu 意为“流行期”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一场流感，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
flu 意为“流感”，指计划里写到、被记录过的那一部分，到 1975 年这一场成了计划里的一行。
flu 意为“流感”，护士二月写道，整件事的流感之事是一间病房和三个星期的记录。
flu 意为“流感”，我记得的是计划里记录过的那一部分，1977 年结束了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一部分。
flu 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，流感是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的东西。
